When two people edit a shared document, saving a whole new copy can replace someone else’s recent work.
A browser based document system where edits travel as small operations, merge on the server, and appear for collaborators.
Keep a shared document consistent while people edit at the same time, with saved history and role based access.
The project also demonstrates how a relational database supports users, workspaces, documents, edit history and permissions.

title: Technical competence: how we built the project

text: Technical competence: how we built the project
We built the application in layers so each part has a clear job.
React and Vite provide the document editor, formatting controls, channel pages and AI writing panel.
Node.js and Express handle sign in, channels, permissions and saved document versions.
Socket.IO carries edit operations and presence updates between people in the same document.
PostgreSQL stores accounts, memberships, documents, operation history and saved versions.
A small character based CRDT was written for this project instead of using a ready made CRDT package.
The team connected the editor to the API and socket events, then checked the CRDT behavior with automated tests.
From sign-in to a shared, saved document, including the project’s AI and language services.

The editor sends grammar, similarity or writing actions through the application server.
LanguageTool checks grammar; a local TF-IDF corpus checks similarity. If LanguageTool is down, one Gemini grammar fallback is attempted with a cooldown.
The server keeps GEMINI_API_KEY private and sends improve, paraphrase, summarize, translate and autocomplete requests. No local generative LLM is included.
REST returns documents, versions and AI responses. Socket.IO broadcasts accepted edits to connected collaborators.
Authorized edits converge through TextCRDT, persist in PostgreSQL and appear in each collaborator’s document.
Evaluation: 13 CRDT unit tests; demonstrate concurrent editing in two sessions.
The editor sends each request to the service that provides that feature.
Grammar, similarity or an AI writing action
LanguageTool checks grammar; local TF-IDF corpus checks text similarity. If LanguageTool is unavailable, one Gemini grammar fallback is attempted with a cooldown.
Keeps GEMINI_API_KEY private; applies per-user rate limits
Improve, paraphrase, summarize, translate and autocomplete
Summary shows an extractive preview. Autocomplete returns no text. Paraphrase and translation show an unavailable message. There is no local generative LLM fallback in this build.
GitHub Pages can host the browser interface only. The API server, database and LanguageTool service must be hosted separately; configure LANGUAGETOOL_URL to reach that service.
PostgreSQL keeps the project’s records connected with foreign keys.

A channel has many members and documents. A document has many operations and versions.
The schema uses unique constraints and indexes for memberships, operation IDs, document lists and version history.
Each inserted character has an ID and a reference to the character before it. Deletes leave a tombstone.
Two people insert after A at nearly the same time

User 1: insert X after A
operation ID: user1:1

User 2: insert Y after A
operation ID: user2:1
Both replicas receive both operations. The CRDT sorts concurrent siblings by operation ID, so delivery order does not decide the result.
A deleted character stays internally as a tombstone so later operations can still refer to its ID.
See who is in a document
Assign admin, editor or viewer roles
Viewers can read; admins and editors can make changes. The server enforces the same rule for API and socket actions.
The main contribution is the way the project combines document management with a custom, inspectable collaboration method.
What is new in this project
Edits are represented as operations instead of replacing the whole text.
The CRDT logic is small enough to inspect and explain in a DBMS project.
Operation history and manual versions make changes easier to review.
More collaborators join through document rooms and channel membership.
New document features can use the existing API, role checks and tables.
Future changes can add tables or modules without changing the core edit flow.
Current scope: one server keeps active CRDTs in memory; this project does not provide offline multi-server synchronization.
We checked correctness at the operation level and build readiness at the application level.
Insert, delete, duplicate IDs, pending dependencies, deterministic order

These checks support the project’s functional claims. They are not a load test or a production reliability study.
A small team can draft and review one shared document without sending files back and forth.
Students can inspect how relational data, permissions, live events and conflict handling fit together.
The current system uses open source tools and a small database schema.
The modular API leaves room for comments, offline support or more document types.
The custom CRDT is educational and runs on one application server.
The originality panel checks against a bundled local corpus; it is not web wide plagiarism detection.
The system is easiest to explain by following one edit from the browser to another user.
Show account access and channel roles
Show the editor and saved content
Watch the second view receive the operation
Preview an older version, then restore it
For accessibility, use a clear spoken sequence, readable text and a live demonstration with prepared accounts and documents.
The project demonstrates a complete path from a user’s edit to a shared, stored document.
The server checks who can edit before it accepts live operations.
The custom CRDT gives replicas a deterministic way to converge.
PostgreSQL stores the document state and its history for later review.
The result is a working educational system that makes its database and collaboration choices visible and explainable.
